test_title: Non-factory states: passwords are unique per device or user-defined.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Complete onboarding → try blank/common defaults on all auth interfaces (UI/API/BLE) → verify first-use change or per-device unique creds.
Evidence: Screenshots of login prompts/results, pcaps of auth attempts, onboarding flow shots, job notes listing all interfaces tried.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: No interface accepts universal/blank/common defaults; first use forces change if preloaded. 
Fail: Any interface authenticates with universal/blank/common creds or proceeds without change.
required_ixit: IXIT 1-AuthMech: ID, Description, Authentication Factor, Password Generation Mechanism

test_title: Robust generation of pre-installed passwords (no patterns, no public-info ties, adequate complexity)
conditions: Pre-installed unique per device passwords are used;
steps_evidence:
Steps: Sample ≥10 devices → record labels/printed secrets → check for serial/pattern correlation → measure length/charset.
Evidence: Photo table (label & S/N masked), spreadsheet of samples with entropy estimate, vendor scheme doc (if provided).
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Each device has a unique secret or enforces first-use change before normal operation. 
Fail: Reused secrets across devices or no enforced change path.
required_ixit: IXIT 1-AuthMech: ID, Description, Authentication Factor, Password Generation Mechanism

test_title: Best-practice cryptography for user authentication
steps_evidence:
Steps: Capture auth traffic (proxy/pcap) → verify TLS/DTLS min versions and no plaintext password → inspect hash/KDF if observable (no plaintext storage).
Evidence: Pcaps with cipher suite/version, screenshots of cert chain and HSTS/pinning (if app), storage excerpts (redacted).
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Weak/short/compromised passwords are rejected per documented policy; secrets stored with strong KDF (no plaintext/reversible). 
Fail: Weak passwords accepted or plaintext/reversible storage observed.
tools: Proxy; Network tools; Certificate inspection; Storage inspection.
required_ixit: IXIT 1-AuthMech: ID, Description, Security Guarantees, Cryptographic Details

test_title: Users can change auth values easily
steps_evidence:
Steps: Change password/API key via UI/app/API → attempt weak passwords → verify policy enforcement and token/session invalidation.
Evidence: UI/app screenshots, API responses, logs showing rejection of weak passwords, session revocation proof.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: User can self-service change credentials (UI/app) after verifying current secret; new value meets policy; old secret and active sessions are invalidated immediately.
Fail: No self-service or change allowed without verification; weak values accepted; old secret still works or sessions persist.
required_ixit: IXIT 1-AuthMech: ID, Description IXIT 2-UserInfo: Documentation of Change Mechanisms

test_title: Brute-force protection
steps_evidence:
Steps: Burst failed logins to threshold → confirm lockout/backoff → verify lockout duration reset behavior.
Evidence: Timestamps of attempts, error messages, server logs, chart of attempt vs response/latency.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: After threshold failures, lockout/backoff is enforced and logged; retry windows sane. 
Fail: Unlimited rapid attempts or trivially bypassed throttling.
required_ixit: IXIT 1-AuthMech: ID, Description, Brute Force Prevention

test_title: Publish a public vuln-disclosure policy with contacts & timelines.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Locate VDP URL in device/app/cloud docs → verify content: contact, scope, timelines, PGP (if any).
Evidence: Screenshots/PDF of VDP page, archived URL, support ticket links.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: VDP page is public, current, and includes intake, scope, timelines, and contacts. 
Fail: No public policy or missing essential elements.
required_ixit: IXIT 2-UserInfo: Publication of Vulnerability Disclosure Policy

test_title: Act on reported vulns in a timely way; implementation confirmed.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Send benign test report via listed channel → measure acknowledgment and triage SLA.
Evidence: Email headers, ticket ID, timestamps, copy of acknowledgment.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Benign report acknowledged within stated SLA; ticket/receipt issued. 
Fail: No acknowledgement or broken channel.
required_ixit: IXIT 2-UserInfo: Publication of Vulnerability Disclosure Policy IXIT 3-VulnTypes: ID, Description, Action, Time Frame IXIT 4-Conf: Confirmation of Vulnerability Actions

test_title: Continuously monitor, identify, and rectify security vulns; implementation confirmed.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Review process doc and change log → verify example fix issuance (CVE/notice).
Evidence: Process doc excerpts, release notes, security advisories.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Process evidence shows triage, remediation, and notice of fixes. 
Fail: No traceable handling or fixes for reported issues.
required_ixit: IXIT 4-Conf: Confirmation of Vulnerability Monitoring IXIT 5-VulnMon: ID, Description

test_title: Components are securely updateable or justifiably not; update mechanisms can’t be misused.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Enumerate updateable components → verify secure path exists or justified not → attempt misuse (e.g., injecting wrong package).
Evidence: Components list, UI/app shots, error logs on misuse.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Secure update path exists (or justified N/A) and rejects misuse (wrong format/path). 
Fail: Components not updatable without justification or path is abusable.
required_ixit: IXIT 6-SoftComp: ID, Description, Update Mechanism IXIT 7-UpdMech: ID, Description, Security Guarantees, Cryptographic Details, Initiation and Interaction

test_title: At least one secure installation mechanism for updates
steps_evidence:
Steps: Trigger update via secure channel → intercept/tamper package → confirm refusal.
Evidence: Pcaps of update session, tamper diff, failure logs.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Update delivery uses TLS/DTLS with correct validation; no plaintext or weak ciphers accepted. 
Fail: Plaintext or invalid/expired/self-signed without pinning is accepted.
required_ixit: IXIT 7-UpdMech: ID, Description, Security Guarantees, Cryptographic Details, Initiation and Interaction

test_title: Simple-to-apply updates available for every component.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Walk through update from user perspective → count steps, required decisions.
Evidence: Step screenshots, timing, any required tools noted.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Each component has a user-accessible, documented update path that completes reliably without special tools.
Fail: Any component lacks an update path or requires service-level access/manual flashing.
required_ixit: IXIT 6-SoftComp: ID, Description, Update Mechanism IXIT 7-UpdMech: ID, Description, Initiation and Interaction

test_title: Automatic checking & installation supported; defaults appropriate.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Verify auto-check schedule and auto-install default → toggle options.
Evidence: Settings screenshots, logs showing auto-check/auto-install events.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Device supports auto-check and (where applicable) auto-install of security updates; defaults prioritize timely security updates.
Fail: No auto-check/install capability or defaults leave security updates effectively disabled.
required_ixit: IXIT 6-SoftComp: ID, Description, Update Mechanism IXIT 7-UpdMech: ID, Description, Initiation and Interaction, Configuration

test_title: Check for security updates after init and periodically.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Observe post-init check and periodic cadence (time offset/cron).
Evidence: Logs with timestamps, config entries.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: An update check occurs after initialization and on a defined periodic cadence per policy (evidence in logs).
Fail: No initial check or no demonstrable periodic cadence.
required_ixit: IXIT 6-SoftComp: ID, Description, Update Mechanism IXIT 7-UpdMech: ID, Description, Update Checking

test_title: User can enable/disable/postpone auto-updates & notifications; sensible defaults.
conditions: The device supports automatic updates and/or update notifications; An update mechanism is implemented;
steps_evidence:
Steps: Enable/disable/postpone auto-update; verify notifications content and timing.
Evidence: Notification screenshots, system logs.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: User can enable/disable/postpone auto-updates and notifications; choices persist; defaults are security-favorable.
Fail: Controls absent/ineffective, state doesn’t persist, or defaults leave users unprotected.
required_ixit: IXIT 7-UpdMech: ID, Description, Initiation and Interaction, Configuration, User Notification

test_title: Best-practice crypto for update channels (integrity & authenticity).
steps_evidence:
Steps: Capture TLS/DTLS; verify version/ciphers, cert validation, pinning (if claimed).
Evidence: Pcaps, certificate chain validation output, pinning behavior proof.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Update transport is encrypted and authenticated (e.g., TLS with cert/hostname validation) and packages enforce integrity/authenticity.
Fail: Plain/weak transport, invalid certs accepted, or no enforced package integrity/authenticity.
tools: Network tools; Proxy; certificate chain verification.
required_ixit: IXIT 7-UpdMech: ID, Description, Security Guarantees, Cryptographic Details

test_title: Management procedures for deploying security updates timely
steps_evidence:
Steps: Obtain an official update package → verify its signature/manifest with the product’s trust anchor (public key, cert chain) → corrupt the package (bit-flip) and retry install → attempt install with a package signed by an untrusted key → observe behavior.
Evidence: Signature-verification logs/output, trust-anchor location/reference (screenshot or config excerpt), hash/manifest files, pcaps of the update session, installer logs showing rejection of tampered or untrusted packages.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Documented process defines roles, risk-based timelines, and tracking; recent security updates meet stated SLAs.
Fail: No defined timelines/process or missed SLAs without justification/evidence.
tools: Binary edtior; Manual inspection; Network tools; Hasing tools; Web browse; Proxy.
required_ixit: IXIT 4-Conf: Confirmation of Update Procedures IXIT 8-UpdProc: ID, Description, Time Frame

test_title: Verification of authenticity/integrity of software update
steps_evidence:
Steps: Attempt to install a downgrade (older version) → attempt to install a package for a different model/region (mismatched metadata) → replay the same version/package when already current → confirm enforcement of model/version checks and anti-rollback/anti-replay controls.
Evidence: Update metadata (model/region/version) screenshots or JSON, installer/update logs showing explicit reject reasons, pcaps or console output from downgrade/replay attempts, before/after version table confirming no rollback occurred.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Downgrades, wrong model/region, or replayed packages are refused with explicit reasons. 
Fail: Older or non-applicable packages install.
tools: Web browser; Debug console; Network tools.
required_ixit: IXIT 7-UpdMech: ID, Description, Security Guarantees, Cryptographic Details

test_title: Trust relationship in network-based update mechanisms is established/verified.
conditions: Updates are delivered over a network interface; An update mechanism is implemented;
steps_evidence:
Steps: Confirm endpoint auth (mTLS/token) and broker trust (if MQTT/CoAP).
Evidence: Broker config, client auth logs, pcaps.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Device verifies the update source (e.g., pinned CA/mTLS/token) and rejects untrusted endpoints/metadata.
Fail: Updates are accepted from unauthenticated or untrusted sources.
required_ixit: IXIT 7-UpdMech: ID, Description, Security Guarantees, Cryptographic Details

test_title: Inform users about available security updates & risk if not applied.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Trigger update availability → check notices explain risk of not updating.
Evidence: UI/app notices, release notes.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Clear user-facing notices announce security updates and state risks of not updating.
Fail: No notification or notices omit risk/importance.
required_ixit: IXIT 7-UpdMech: ID, Description, User Notification

test_title: Notify users before disruptive update actions on the device.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Initiate disruptive update → verify warning and user consent.
Evidence: Warning dialog, user confirmation, schedule options.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Users are notified before disruptive actions (reboot/downtime) with schedule/deferral options.
Fail: Disruptive updates occur without advance notice or user control.
required_ixit: IXIT 7-UpdMech: ID, Description, User Notification

test_title: Publish support period for security updates.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Locate support window/EoL statement.
Evidence: Policy screenshot/PDF, product page archive.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Publicly available support/EoL window for security updates for the model.
Fail: No published support period or unclear/hidden information.
required_ixit: IXIT 2-UserInfo: Support Period, Publication of Support Period

test_title: If updates stop/aren’t possible: give rationale & replacement guidance.
conditions: Software components are not updateable; The device is constrained;
steps_evidence:
Steps: Verify rationale and replacement/mitigation guidance.
Evidence: Notice text, migration guide.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Vendor provides rationale and clear replacement/mitigation guidance at/ before EoL.
Fail: Updates cease without notice, rationale, or mitigation guidance.
required_ixit: IXIT 2-UserInfo: Documentation of Replacement, Publication of Non-Updatable

test_title: Support component isolation and replacement where applicable.
conditions: Software components are not updateable; The device is constrained;
steps_evidence:
Steps: Show modular update of a component (e.g., app vs firmware).
Evidence: Update logs showing isolated component change.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Components can be updated/replaced independently; isolation documented and functional.
Fail: Monolithic updates only; component replacement unsupported or breaks other functions.
required_ixit: IXIT 9-ReplSup: Isolation, Hardware Replacement

test_title: Make model designation easily available for users.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Check model/firmware identifiers are easily accessible in UI/label/app.
Evidence: Photos/screenshots of model/version fields.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Model identifier and firmware/software version are easy to find (label/UI/app) for update decisions.
Fail: Model/version info is missing or not user-accessible.
required_ixit: IXIT 2-UserInfo: Model Designation

test_title: Secure storage of sensitive security parameters
conditions: Sensitive security parameters are stored persistently;
steps_evidence:
Steps: Inventory CSPs (keys/tokens/passwords) → verify storage scheme (KDF/keystore/TEE) → attempt read/export via normal interfaces.
Evidence: CSP inventory table, config/DB excerpts (redacted), failure logs on export.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: User secrets hashed with strong KDF; no plaintext/reversible storage of CSPs. 
Fail: Plaintext/reversible hashes or exportable secrets.
tools: Debug consoles; Database inspection; Extraction tools.
required_ixit: IXIT 10-SecParam: ID, Description, Type, Security Guarantees, Protection Scheme

test_title: Tamper-resistant storage for hard-coded device identities
conditions: A hard-coded unique per device identity is used for security purposes;
steps_evidence:
Steps: Identify device identities (IDs/certs) → confirm hardware anchor (TPM/SE/TEE) or protection → test copy/clone prevention.
Evidence: Hardware/SoC docs, API behavior screenshots, clone attempt log.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Identities/keys anchored in tamper-resistant/immutable storage (SE/TPM/TEE/ROM/eFuse), non-exportable and non-overwritable; cloned identities are rejected.
Fail: Identities/keys are readable/modifiable via normal/debug paths, or a cloned identity is accepted.
tools: Debug console; Manual inspection; Extraction tools.
required_ixit: IXIT 10-SecParam: ID, Description, Type, Security Guarantees, Protection Scheme

test_title: No runtime use of hard-coded critical security parameters
steps_evidence:
Steps: Static/firmware scan for embedded secrets → dynamic runtime check for hard-coded use.
Evidence: Scan report, code strings (redacted), runtime traces.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Firmware/app images contain no embedded credentials/API keys used in production. 
Fail: Hard-coded production secrets present/usable.
tools: Extraction tools; Disassembler; Emulators; Debug console.
required_ixit: IXIT 10-SecParam: ID, Description, Type, Provisioning Mechanism

test_title: Per-device generation of critical security parameters with sufficient entropy
conditions: Critical security parameters used for integrity and authenticity checks of software updates in device software or for protection of communication with associated services in device software exist;
steps_evidence:
Steps: Review keygen/CSR process → sample randomness source → ensure non-predictability.
Evidence: Entropy source doc, sample distribution summary, generation logs.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: CSPs are generated per device using a CSPRNG seeded by hardware entropy; adequate key sizes; no correlation with serial/metadata; no reuse observed.
Fail: Secrets are predictable/derived from serial/MAC, reused across devices, or generated with insufficient entropy/key length.
required_ixit: IXIT 10-SecParam: ID, Description, Type, Generation Mechanism

test_title: Use best-practice cryptography for communications
steps_evidence:
Steps: Capture all channels (app, cloud, local) → verify TLS/DTLS version/ciphers; check downgrade resistance.
Evidence: Pcaps, cipher suite list, server banners, rejection of weak ciphers.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Only secure protocol versions/cipher suites are accepted; weak/legacy are refused. 
Fail: Outdated versions/ciphers accepted.
tools: Web browser; Network tools; Manual inspection; Proxy.
required_ixit: IXIT 11-ComMech: ID, Description, Security Guarantees, Cryptographic Details

test_title: Review/evaluate network & security implementations
steps_evidence:
Steps: Collect vendor security reports → confirm match to device name/version → sample claim verification in lab.
Evidence: Vendor report copy, cross-check notes, test confirmation.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: A current security review/report exists for the exact model/version; key claims are spot-checked and match behavior; issues are tracked to closure.
Fail: No review, outdated/mismatched report, or claims cannot be verified in testing.
required_ixit: IXIT 12-NetSecImpl: ID, Description, Review/Evaluation Method, Report

test_title: Crypto agility: components updateable
steps_evidence:
Steps: Verify components are updateable and algorithm sets configurable; simulate deprecation scenario (e.g., disable SHA-1).
Evidence: Settings screenshots, post-change connectivity logs.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Crypto libraries/suites/keys can be updated or migrated away from deprecated algorithms without factory return.
Fail: Fixed crypto that cannot be updated or reliance on deprecated/weak algorithms with no migration path.
tools: Web browser; Network tools; Manual inspection; Proxy.
required_ixit: IXIT 6-SoftComp: ID, Description, Update Mechanism, Cryptographic Usage IXIT 7-UpdMech: ID, Description

test_title: Auth required for network-accessible functions
conditions: Access to device functionality via a network interface in the initialized state is possible;
steps_evidence:
Steps: Attempt unauth actions → verify auth required; test role separation.
Evidence: 401/403 responses, role matrix, logs.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: All network-reachable functions require authentication; least-privilege roles enforced; unauth actions are blocked.
Fail: Any sensitive function is usable without auth or privileges are trivially bypassed.
required_ixit: IXIT 1-AuthMech: ID, Description, Security Guarantees, Cryptographic Details IXIT 13-SoftServ: ID, Description, Authentication Mechanism

test_title: Auth for security-relevant configuration
conditions: Device functionality that allows security-relevant changes in configuration via a network interface exists;
steps_evidence:
Steps: Change critical settings with/without auth → scan for hidden endpoints/services.
Evidence: Scan results, config change logs, access denials.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Security-relevant settings require an authenticated, authorized role; no undocumented services enable such changes.
Fail: Security settings changeable without proper auth/authorization, or hidden endpoints/services permit it.
required_ixit: IXIT 1-AuthMech: ID, Description, Security Guarantees, Cryptographic Details IXIT 13-SoftServ: ID, Description, Allows Configuration, Authentication Mechanism

test_title: Encrypt critical security parameters in transit
steps_evidence:
Steps: Intercept flows carrying CSPs → confirm encrypted and integrity-protected.
Evidence: Pcaps showing no plaintext CSPs, API response signatures.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: CSPs (keys/tokens/passwords) are transmitted only over authenticated, integrity-protected channels; no plaintext exposure.
Fail: CSPs observed in clear/weakly protected transit or without integrity checks.
required_ixit: IXIT 10-SecParam: ID, Description, Type, Communication Mechanisms IXIT 11-ComMech: ID, Description, Security Guarantees, Cryptographic Details

test_title: Encrypt critical security parameters over remote interfaces
conditions: Critical security parameters are transmitted via remotely accessible network interfaces;
steps_evidence:
Steps: Test remote admin interfaces (WAN/cloud) for enforced encryption.
Evidence: TLS info, HSTS/pinning, failed downgrade attempts.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Remote/WAN/cloud admin interfaces always enforce strong encryption and endpoint validation for CSP exchange.
Fail: Remote interfaces allow or fall back to plaintext/invalid-cert connections for CSPs.
required_ixit: IXIT 10-SecParam: ID, Description, Type, Communication Mechanisms IXIT 11-ComMech: ID, Description, Security Guarantees, Cryptographic Details

test_title: Secure lifecycle management of critical security parameters
conditions: Critical security parameters relating to the device exist;
steps_evidence:
Steps: Review generate→provision→rotate→revoke→decommission → execute a rotation/revocation.
Evidence: Key rotation logs, revoked credential no longer accepted, audit entries.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Documented processes exist and are enforced for CSP generation, provisioning, rotation, revocation, and decommission; revoked/rotated secrets become unusable.
Fail: No lifecycle controls; stale/revoked secrets still work or cannot be rotated/revoked.
required_ixit: IXIT 4-Conf: Confirmation of Secure Management IXIT 14-SecMgmt: ID, Description

test_title: Enable only justified network/logical interfaces
steps_evidence:
Steps: Enumerate network/physical interfaces → compare to IXIT → justify each enabled one.
Evidence: Port scan results, interface table with justifications.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Only necessary services/ports exposed; inventory matches IXIT; filtering applied as stated. 
Fail: Unjustified or undocumented exposed services.
tools: Manual inspection; Debug console; Network tools; Web browser; Proxy.
required_ixit: IXIT 15-Intf: ID, Description, Type, Status

test_title: Limits unauthenticated network disclosures to what’s necessary for operation
steps_evidence:
Steps: Observe unauthenticated banners/APIs → verify minimal info.
Evidence: Anonymous query responses, diffs before/after hardening.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Unauthenticated requests expose only minimal, non-sensitive info needed for operation; versions/serials/config/PII and verbose errors are suppressed.
Fail: Unauthenticated requests reveal versions, identifiers, configs, user/telemetry data, or detailed error messages.
tools: Manual inspection; Debug console; Network tools; Web browser; Proxy.
required_ixit: IXIT 15-Intf: ID, Description, Type, Disclosed Information

test_title: Protect non-required physical/air interfaces (casing or disable)
steps_evidence:
Steps: Inspect PCB/case → check BLE/AP modes → verify disabled or protected when not needed.
Evidence: Photos, radio scan results, config flags.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Non-required physical/air radios are disabled, fused, or physically blocked; use attempts fail on production units.
Fail: Unneeded pads/headers or radios remain accessible/active, enabling console/pairing without authorization.
required_ixit: IXIT 15-Intf: ID, Description, Type, Status, Protection

test_title: Control debug interfaces via software; permanently disabled or default-disabled; no undocumented debug ports
conditions: A debug interface is physically accessible;
steps_evidence:
Steps: Probe UART/JTAG/SWD → confirm locked or disabled → attempt enablement (should fail by default).
Evidence: Probe logs, failure traces, photos.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: UART/JTAG/SWD non-functional or fully access-controlled on production units. 
Fail: Unauthenticated or trivially enabled debug grants shell/bootloader/memory access.
required_ixit: IXIT 15-Intf: ID, Description, Type, Status, Debug Interface, Protection

test_title: Minimize enabled services
steps_evidence:
Steps: Service inventory → disable non-essential → retest exposure.
Evidence: Before/after service lists, config diffs.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Only documented, necessary services/ports are enabled by default; others are removed or filtered by firewall.
Fail: Undocumented or unnecessary services are reachable, or defaults expose extra ports.
tools: Manual inspection; Debug console; Network scanners; Web browser; Proxy.
required_ixit: IXIT 13-SoftServ: ID, Description, Status, Justification

test_title: Apply proportionate code-minimization techniques
steps_evidence:
Steps: Review build/firmware for stripped features/deps; check package lists.
Evidence: Manifest/package list, size reduction metrics.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Unused packages/features/debug code removed; production image is minimal (no sample apps/backdoors).
Fail: Dead code, test endpoints, sample apps, or unused interpreters remain in production builds.
required_ixit: IXIT 16-CodeMin: ID, Description

test_title: Enforce least-privilege & separation of duties
steps_evidence:
Steps: Validate role permissions and process privileges (UID/GID/caps).
Evidence: RBAC configs, process listings, denied action logs.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Roles/processes run with least privileges; privileged actions require authorization; duties are separated.
Fail: Services run as root/admin without need, or roles permit broad access/privilege escalation.
required_ixit: IXIT 17-PrivlCtrl: ID, Description

test_title: Provide hardware-level memory access control mechanisms
steps_evidence:
Steps: Verify MMU/MPU protections; attempt out-of-range access (expected fail).
Evidence: Kernel/device logs, exception traces.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: MMU/MPU and NX/W^X/IOMMU (as applicable) configured; unauthorized reads/writes are blocked.
Fail: Writable-executable regions, unrestricted DMA, or missing region protections allow unauthorized access.
required_ixit: IXIT 18-AccCtrl: ID, Description

test_title: Implement a secure development lifecycle
steps_evidence:
Steps: Review SDLC artifacts (training, threat models, code reviews, SAST/DAST, SBOM) → sample a release trail.
Evidence: Training records, review tickets, SAST/DAST reports, SBOM snapshot.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Documented SDL includes training, threat modeling, code review, SAST/DAST, SBOM/dependency management, and release sign-off; evidence exists for current version.
Fail: No SDL artifacts or security gates; third-party components unmanaged or untracked.
required_ixit: IXIT 4-Conf: Confirmation of Secure Development IXIT 19-SecDev: ID, Description

test_title: Secure boot verifies integrity & authenticity of device software.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Attempt boot with unsigned/modified image → observe refusal → verify rollback path.
Evidence: Boot logs/console output, hash/signature records, tamper diff.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Modified/unsigned images fail to boot; only trusted-signed images load; rollback path secure. 
Fail: Untrusted images boot or verification disabled by non-privileged means.
required_ixit: IXIT 20-SecBoot: ID, Description, Security Guarantees, Detection Mechanisms

test_title: On detecting unauthorized software change: alert and restrict communications to what’s strictly necessary.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Induce integrity failure → confirm alerting and minimal comms mode.
Evidence: Alerts (UI/app/syslog), network capture showing restricted traffic.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Unauthorized modification triggers detection/logging and restricts functionality/communications. 
Fail: Runtime tamper not detected or no restriction applied.
tools: Network tools; Web browser; Manual inspection; Debug console.
required_ixit: IXIT 20-SecBoot: ID, Description, User Notification, Notification Functionality

test_title: Best-practice crypto for personal-data communications.
conditions: Personal data is transmitted between a device and a service;
steps_evidence:
Steps: Capture flows with personal data → confirm encryption and cert validation.
Evidence: Pcaps, TLS details, data classification table.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Sensitive personal data protected (encryption or strict access control) with authorization checks. 
Fail: Sensitive data readable without authorization or stored unprotected.
required_ixit: IXIT 11-ComMech: ID, Description, Security Guarantees, Cryptographic Details IXIT 21-PersData: ID, Description, Communication Mechanisms

test_title: Best-practice crypto for sensitive personal-data communications.
conditions: Sensitive personal data is transmitted between a device and a service;
steps_evidence:
Steps: Repeat for sensitive categories (health, biometrics) with stricter controls.
Evidence: Pcaps, policy mappings for sensitivity.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: Sensitive data sent only over authenticated, modern crypto (e.g., TLS with cert/hostname validation); integrity protected; no plaintext in URLs/logs/cache.
Fail: Sensitive data observed in clear or via weak crypto, or connections proceed with invalid/mismatched certs.
required_ixit: IXIT 11-ComMech: ID, Description, Security Guarantees, Cryptographic Details IXIT 21-PersData: ID, Description, Processing Activities, Communication Mechanisms, Sensitive

test_title: Document external sensing capabilities clearly for users.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Check documentation/UI for sensors (mic/cam/GNSS) disclosure.
Evidence: Manual/app screenshots, onboarding disclosures.
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: UI/docs explicitly list sensors (e.g., mic/cam/GNSS), purpose, data use, and user controls; description matches behavior.
Fail: Sensors not disclosed, info incomplete/misleading, or behavior contradicts documentation.
required_ixit: IXIT 2-UserInfo: Documentation of Sensors IXIT 22-ExtSens: ID, Description

test_title: Resilience mechanisms are appropriate for network/power outages.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Simulate network/power outages → observe failover/queueing/retry.
Evidence: Event logs with timestamps, state diagrams (if provided).
acceptance_criteria:
Pass: On loss/restoration, device behaves safely, preserves integrity, and resumes expected operation. 
Fail: Unsafe states, data loss, or insecure defaults on recovery.
required_ixit: IXIT 23-ResMech: ID, Description, Security Guarantees

test_title: Operate locally during network loss & recover cleanly after power loss.
steps_evidence:
Steps: Use device locally during WAN loss → power cycle mid-operation → confirm no insecure defaults on recovery.

test_title: Side-Channel & Fault-Injection — screening level
steps_evidence:
Steps (screening, non-destructive):
1-Baseline & Triggering — Record normal operation for each target function (golden traces, timestamps, UART logs). Verify stable triggers and DUT repeatability.
2-Passive SCA Screening — Capture short runs of power/EM traces around the target function while varying non-sensitive inputs minimally; look for obvious, repeatable correlation/leakage patterns (qualitative only at screening level).
3-Plan FI Windows — From the baseline timing, define conservative windows where a fault might influence the target check (pre-check, compare, branch). Document planned windows and step sizes.
4-Clock Glitch Screening — Apply low-energy, short-duration timing perturbations across the defined window (coarse sweep). Observe DUT behavior (reset, error, hang, pass/fail outcome).
5-Voltage Glitch Screening — Within safe envelopes, apply brief supply perturbations (coarse sweep). Monitor device state and logs; immediately abort on abnormal thermals/overcurrent.
6-EM Transient Screening (optional) — Apply low-energy EM pulses while scanning across the package area (coarse grid) and timing window.
7-Reproduce Interesting Effects — If any anomalous behavior suggests security-relevant impact (e.g., signature check unexpectedly “passes,” lockout skipped), attempt to reproduce ≥3 times with the same parameters.
8-Containment & Health Check — After each series, verify DUT still boots and functions normally; compare hash/version to pre-test; reset to golden state if needed.
9-Cleanup — Restore default settings; remove probes; document any persistent side effects and notify TM/client per PR-NC-01 if nonconforming work is suspected.

Evidence to Capture:
-Test matrix (date/time, operator, target function, trigger, window, parameters, repetitions, outcomes).
-Setup photos (probe points, shielding), wiring diagram, and risk/safety checklist.
-Baseline (“golden”) traces and representative SCA/FI traces (file paths + checksums).
-DUT console logs/UART captures; application/system logs; any network pcaps if behavior is network-visible.
-Tool configs & versions; environment notes (temp, supply voltage).
-Firmware/boot image identifiers and hashes used during testing.
-Reproducibility record (attempts vs. successes), severity rating, and any hypothesized mechanism (qualitative).
-Post-test health verification (functional checks, version/hash unchanged).
acceptance_criteria:
Pass (screening): No reproducible bypass or safety-relevant malfunction within defined screening envelopes; any observed leakage is documented qualitatively with no key or credential extraction attempted.
Finding: A reproducible effect that degrades a security control (e.g., bypass of verification, lockout defeat) within screening envelopes → record as a finding under this LD method (outside ETSI EN/TS conformance scope), with recommended mitigations.
required_ixit: IXIT: permitted stress limits; safety constraints
